name: Lanthanum barium cuprate, x = 0.115
equilibrium_context: Tc = 13 K, three-dimensional superconductivity strongly suppressed by stripe order; spin order at 40 K

driven_states.emergent_property: Near-infrared excitation blue-shifts the Josephson plasma resonance below Tc and creates, above Tc, a plasma edge that is absent in equilibrium, up to the spin-ordering temperature of 40 K. In a field of 7 T the transient interlayer phase coherence length grows by up to a factor of ten.

drive.polarization: E perpendicular to the CuO2 planes markedly more effective

driven_states.source: Nicoletti et al., Phys. Rev. B 90, 100503 (2014), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.90.100503
driven_states.caveat: Two independent groups (MPSD Hamburg, UCSD/BNL) report positive signatures, which is why reproduced would be defensible. Downgraded to contested because Zhang et al., using near-infrared pumping on the closely related composition x = 0.125, explicitly find no transient three-dimensional superconductivity. Cremin et al. themselves speak only of enhanced superconducting fluctuations. No transport, no Meissner evidence.
further_sources: Casandruc et al., Phys. Rev. B 91, 174502 (2015), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.91.174502
Nicoletti et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 267003 (2018), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.267003
Cremin et al., PNAS 116, 19875 (2019), doi:10.1073/pnas.1908368116 (independent group)
Counter-position: Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. X 14, 011036 (2024), doi:10.1103/PhysRevX.14.011036
driven_states.measured_quantity: c-axis THz reflection; magnetic field dependence of the coherence length

sources: Nicoletti et al., Phys. Rev. B 90, 100503 (2014), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.90.100503
gaps: Lifetime reported between 1e-11 s (MPSD) and more than 3e-10 s (Cremin), depending on the method.
